body.statement: For every law \(P\), consistency and event-date counterfactual transport alone imply \(\tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]-m_s(z_{0s})\}\).
body.justification: This isolates causal identification from the estimation frontier and keeps the target a level-wealth contrast rather than a return approximation.
body.gap: Ferman (2021) obtains factor-loading recovery for synthetic controls; it does not identify this nonlinear realized-path wealth regression functional.
body.consumer: Financial event studies can report an interpretable dollar-wealth effect while using rolling untreated pseudo-events only to diagnose or falsify pre-event stability, not to verify event-date transport.
body.proof_tex:
By \texttt{def:target},
\[
 \tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
 \left\{\mathbb E[B_{si}(1)\mid z_0]
             -\mathbb E[B_{si}(0)\mid z_0]\right\}.                 \tag{1}
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:consistency} gives
\(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{si}(1)\) almost surely, hence equality of the
corresponding conditional expectations at every query value where the
chosen regular conditional expectations are defined:
\[
 \mathbb E[B_{si}(1)\mid z_0]
 =\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0].                          \tag{2}
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:event-date-transport} separately gives
\[
 \mathbb E[B_{si}(0)\mid z_0]=m_s(z_{0s}).                           \tag{3}
\]
Substituting (2)--(3) into the finite sum (1) proves
\[
 \tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
 \left\{\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]-m_s(z_{0s})\right\}.
\]
Thus the observed-law functional is derived from the causal contrast and is
not its definition.  No design-density, mixing, donor, rank, or inversion
condition is used.
